text: Who or what is the lady in black so afraid of? — whoever now controls her income
why: The lady is terrified, has no one to turn to, and her income is controlled by someone she will escape by marrying, so the controller is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: Does the lady in black belong to the Roylotts of Stoke Moran?
why: ¶1 introduces the Roylotts of Stoke Moran, so the question is a fair one to ask.

text: Does the lady in black belong to the Roylotts of Stoke Moran? — she has no tie to the family
id: q.lady_roylotts=she has no tie to the family
why: Asserts she has no tie to the Roylotts, which the story never states and no reader could yet rule out.

text: What has Dr. Grimesby Roylott to do with the lady's trouble?
why: ¶1 links Roylott's death to the matter, so asking his connection to the lady's trouble is a fair question.

text: What has Dr. Grimesby Roylott to do with the lady's trouble? — he controls her income and is what she fears
id: q.roylott_in_trouble=he controls her income and is what she fears
why: Names Roylott as the controller of her income and the one she fears; nothing so far connects him to her or her money.

text: What has Dr. Grimesby Roylott to do with the lady's trouble? — he is threatened alongside her
why: Says Roylott is threatened alongside her; nothing in the story so far hints at any threat to him.

text: What has Dr. Grimesby Roylott to do with the lady's trouble? — he is only incidental to her trouble
id: q.roylott_in_trouble=he is only incidental to her trouble
why: Whether Roylott is involved at all is an open question the story has raised, so 'only incidental' is a legitimate possibility to consider.

text: Who has the control of the lady's income until she marries?
why: Plain question: she says she will control her own income after marriage, implying someone else controls it now.

text: Who has the control of the lady's income until she marries? — a guardian or trustee not yet mentioned
id: q.who_holds_income=a guardian or trustee not yet mentioned
why: Her income is controlled by someone unnamed, so a guardian or trustee is a reasonable possibility.

text: Who is the one person who cares for the lady?
why: ¶17 says there is one person who cares for her.

text: Who is the one person who cares for the lady? — the man she is to marry
id: q.one_who_cares=the man she is to marry
why: She mentions an upcoming marriage and the caring person is unnamed, so this is a reasonable possibility.

text: Who is the one person who cares for the lady? — a relative of hers
why: The caring person is unidentified, so a relative is a reasonable possibility.

text: Why can the one who cares for her be of so little aid?
why: ¶17 says 'he, poor fellow, can be of little aid', so the question is a plain one.

text: Why can the one who cares for her be of so little aid? — he is ill or infirm
why: Illness or infirmity is a general possibility for why someone can offer little aid.

text: Why can the one who cares for her be of so little aid? — he is absent
why: Absence is a general possibility for why someone can offer little aid.

text: Why can the one who cares for her be of so little aid? — he is poor and powerless
why: 'Poor fellow' and 'little aid' make poverty and powerlessness a reasonable possibility.
